reviewer: Codex direct visual inspection of the three formal stills and all 48 formal contact-clip frames

answers.question: Does the hero read as one designed guardian robot rather than a stack of primitive shapes and attached panels?
answers.rationale: The wide and close shots preserve a coherent black-armored guardian silhouette, consistent cyan/coral accents and an organized face. The asset remains prototype-grade and blocky, but it reads as one character rather than unrelated primitives.

answers.question: Does the wide shot preserve chamber depth, aperture, floor and atmosphere while keeping the hero silhouette readable?
answers.rationale: The coral aperture, concentric chamber rings, floor pool of light and atmospheric darkness remain visible while the guardian and console silhouette stay separable.

answers.question: Does the medium shot hold 0.48–0.72 occupancy and clearly show the hand-to-control action?
answers.rationale: The measured occupancy is 0.52000001. The contact-normal view holds the local hand, housing and cyan plunger together; the 48-frame sequence makes the press unambiguous.

answers.question: Does the close shot show at least four organized facial landmarks instead of one dominant coral side pod?
answers.rationale: Five organized cyan/dark landmarks form brow, eye line, cheeks and jaw. The face occupies the frame and the coral side pod is only a small edge element.

answers.question: Does the visible hand collider make continuous physical contact without a gap or obvious penetration?
answers.rationale: Across the formal contact frames the visible hand closes onto the plunger continuously; there is no visible teleport, sustained gap or gross intersection.

answers.question: Does the spring control compress, reverse and settle continuously under Bullet rather than jumping between authored poses?
answers.rationale: The plunger visibly recedes under the hand, reverses after peak compression and returns toward equilibrium continuously. The machine receipt binds the same sequence to zero mechanism pose keys.

answers.question: Does measured native blur add speed without hiding hand, control, face or contact direction?
answers.rationale: Peak motion carries a restrained native blur trace while hand contour, plunger direction and console edge remain readable; the later face shot is sharp.

answers.question: Does the solver-owned mechanism outcome look supported and mechanically plausible rather than arranged?
answers.rationale: The plunger sits inside a fixed circular housing on the console, moves only along the support-normal spring axis and returns without an authored final pose.

answers.question: Are the accepted lighting and shot-progression strengths preserved?
answers.rationale: The blue/coral contrast, chamber aperture, rim highlights and wide-to-contact-to-reaction progression are preserved and made causally clearer.

limitations: Robot body modeling, surface breakup and material richness remain prototype-grade rather than photoreal or advertising-grade.
The authored full-body performance remains simple; RC1 validates the hybrid intention/contact-response boundary, not broad character acting.
The medium is intentionally a tight contact insert and relies on the clip, not its peak still alone, to communicate compression and rebound.
